transitivity.subtitle: Transitive & Intransitive Verb Pairs
transitivity.transitiveExplain: An agent deliberately acts on an object marked with を. The sentence names who or what caused the action.
transitivity.intransitiveExplain: The subject, marked with が, changes or ends up in a state by itself, no agent is named. Often the more tactful choice, since it avoids assigning blame.
transitivity.exampleTransitiveCaption: Someone opened the window. (names the agent)
transitivity.exampleIntransitiveCaption: The window is open. (no agent named)
transitivity.chapterTieIn: Chapter 19 · How this connects to てある / ている / ておく
transitivity.teAruNote: Transitive verb + てある, with が: describes a resultant state someone deliberately created. Implies purpose.
transitivity.teIruNote: Intransitive verb + ている: just describes the current state. Doesn't necessarily imply anyone's intent.
transitivity.teOkuNote: Transitive verb + ておく: describes the preparatory ACTION itself ("do it in advance/for later"), from the doer's point of view, not covered as its own grammar point yet, but built from the same transitive verb as てある.
transitivity.chapterTieInFooter: N4 chapter 19 (自動詞と他動詞) is exactly this contrast: Nを+他動詞 vs N（は／が）+自動詞, then てある layered onto the transitive verb for a deliberate resultant state. Tap a pattern below to jump to its full entry in Grammar.

tabs.particles: Which particle goes with the verb

intro.synonyms: Words that translate to the same Vietnamese/English gloss but split on use-case in Japanese, which one you reach for depends on the object, the body part, or the register, not the dictionary meaning.
intro.particles: A verb's particle is often fixed by the verb itself, not by logic borrowed from English, these are the strict pairings and exceptions worth memorizing as fixed chunks, including a few で/を surprises.
intro.auxiliary: Auxiliary verbs riding on the て-form add a layer of nuance, completion, regret, trial, preparation, direction, on top of the main verb's plain meaning.
